questions.q: What is the brick position shown, a unit laid on its long edge with its broad face showing on the wall surface?
questions.n: A shiner is laid on its long edge with the broad face exposed in the wall.

questions.q: In concrete mix proportioning, which property is governed by the water-cement ratio?
questions.n: Per Abrams' law, a lower water-cement ratio generally produces higher compressive strength, so w/c ratio is the main control on strength.

questions.q: A concrete cylinder tested early gave 1,400 psi. What compressive strength should the concrete reach at full cure?
questions.n: An early-age (e.g., 7-day) result is usually only 65-70% of the eventual 28-day strength. Backing that out from 1,400 psi gives an expected 28-day strength near 2,100 psi.

questions.q: Which of these floor types demands the strictest levelness and flatness?
questions.n: Warehouses using air-pallet or air-caster handling ride on a very thin air film that is extremely sensitive to floor irregularities, generally making this the strictest flatness requirement of the group.

questions.q: Which of these rock types is igneous?
questions.n: Granite is igneous, formed as molten magma cools and crystallizes.

questions.q: Among the glazing types below, which does the least to cut down noise transmission?
questions.n: Double-strength glass is just one thicker single pane, so it gives almost no acoustic improvement. Double glazing, insulating glass, and laminated glass all add a second pane or a damping interlayer that cuts sound transmission better.

questions.q: When the Contractor is permitted to choose whether or not to act, which word is used?
questions.n: "May" signals that the Contractor has discretion to exercise an option rather than being required to act.

questions.q: For dimension lumber 8 inches and larger, how much smaller is the actual (dressed) size than the nominal size?
questions.n: Under the American Softwood Lumber Standard, nominal sizes of 8 inches and up are dressed down by 3/4 inch to reach actual size (versus 1/2 inch for widths under 8 inches).

questions.q: In the roof identification figure, point "D" marks the internal line where two roof slopes meet and channel water downward. What is it called?
questions.n: An internal intersection where two roof slopes meet, forming a "V" that channels water down, is a valley — seen where the dormer roof meets the main roof at point D.

questions.q: What term describes any wedge-shaped unit in a masonry arch or vault, cut so its sides converge toward the arch center?
questions.n: A voussoir is any wedge-shaped masonry unit forming an arch or vault, with sides converging toward the arch's center.

questions.q: All but one of the choices describe what sealers are for. Which one is NOT a sealer function?
o: Providing a firm bond between a substrate and the coats applied over it
Stopping subsequent coatings from being absorbed by the substrate
Keeping materials from penetrating into or leaching out of a substrate
Protecting subsequent coatings from substances present in the substrate
questions.n: Bonding a substrate to the coats above it is a primer's job. A sealer's defining role is blocking, containing, or isolating substances in the substrate so they don't affect the coating system.

questions.q: What describes a flat or pitched truss where the vertical members carry compression and the diagonals carry tension?
questions.n: In a Pratt truss, verticals carry compression and diagonals carry tension.

questions.q: Which property below best describes wood?
questions.n: Wood is anisotropic — its strength, shrinkage, and other properties change depending on direction relative to the grain.

questions.q: Which metallic-coated carbon steel roofing panel is coated with a blend of aluminum and zinc?
questions.n: Galvalume is coated with an aluminum-zinc alloy (roughly 55% aluminum, 43.5% zinc).

questions.q: When a product, system, or process is specified by a particular make — especially a registered trademark — what is that specification called?
questions.n: A specific product tied to a registered trademark or brand is described in specifications as "proprietary."

questions.q: Sawn lumber shrinks and distorts differently depending on where in the log it was cut. Which cutting method gives the least distortion?
questions.n: Quarter-sawn lumber, cut radially from the log, is the most dimensionally stable and distorts the least compared with plain-sawn or rotary-cut lumber.

questions.q: In the roof identification figure, point "A" marks the sloped line where two roof planes meet at an outside corner. What is it called?
questions.n: An external sloped intersection where two roof planes meet at an outside corner is a hip — the diagonal roof-to-roof edge at point A.

questions.q: Brick and structural tile can be shaped by pushing plastic clay through a die and wire-cutting it to length before firing. What is this forming method called?
questions.n: The stiff-mud process extrudes a stiff clay column through a die and wire-cuts it to length before firing — the most common way brick and tile are formed.

questions.q: A Class C (1:3:6) concrete mix used 15 bags of cement for a pour. How much gravel does that call for?
questions.n: Typical Philippine mix proportions for Class C (1:3:6) use about 6 bags of cement and 1.0 m³ of gravel per m³ of concrete. Fifteen bags corresponds to roughly 15/6 ≈ 2.5 m³ of concrete, so about 2.5 cu.m of gravel is needed.

questions.q: What describes a flat or bowstring truss whose inclined web members form a series of near-equilateral triangles?
questions.n: A Belgian truss is a flat or bowstring truss whose web members form a series of equilateral, or nearly equilateral, triangles.

questions.q: In a lumber specification, what does "S4S" mean?
questions.n: S4S means "Surfaced (smoothed) on Four Sides" — lumber that has been machine-planed smooth on every face.

questions.q: What is the joint called that forms when one concrete pour hardens before the next batch is placed against it?
questions.n: A cold joint forms when concrete hardens, or starts to set, before the next batch is placed against it, leaving a visible plane of weakness.

questions.q: What is the opening through a parapet called that lets water drain off the edge of a flat roof?
questions.n: A scupper is an opening through a parapet wall that lets water drain off the edge of a flat roof.

questions.q: In structural steel, what does the abbreviation "HSS" stand for?
questions.n: HSS refers to Hollow Structural Sections — round, square, or rectangular tubular steel members.

questions.q: What is a plate structure made of thin, deep elements rigidly joined at angles along their edges, each bracing its neighbor against lateral buckling?
questions.n: A folded-plate structure consists of thin, deep planar elements rigidly joined at angles, with each plate bracing the next against buckling.

questions.q: Which of these rock types is sedimentary?
questions.n: Limestone is sedimentary, built up from compacted mineral and organic sediment, often calcium carbonate.

questions.q: Which construction method is regarded as the most basic among these building types?
questions.n: Wood light-frame ("stick-built") construction relies on simple, widely available materials and basic tools, making it the simplest and most common method listed.

questions.q: When the Contractor must pick from a limited, specified set of alternatives, which phrase is used?
questions.n: "Shall either… or" is used when the Contractor must select among a defined, limited set of alternatives.

questions.q: A door's knob sits on the left, and the leaf swings out and away from the room. What hand is this door?
questions.n: Door "hand" is judged standing on the side the door swings away from. A left-knob door swinging outward toward that person is Left Hand Reverse.

questions.q: What is the brick position shown, a brick laid on its long edge with only its end face showing on the wall surface?
questions.n: A rowlock brick is laid on its long edge with just the end face exposed in the wall.

questions.q: What do you call a beam running along the outer edge of a floor or roof?
questions.n: A spandrel beam runs along the outer perimeter of a floor or roof framing plan.

questions.q: Moisture pulls dissolved salts to a masonry surface, where evaporation and sun heat leave a white residue that must be cleaned off before painting. What is this residue called?
questions.n: Efflorescence is the powdery white salt deposit left on masonry when moisture carries dissolved salts to the surface and evaporates.

questions.q: What is the name for a semi-cylindrical shingle-type roof tile laid in courses, alternating convex-side-up and convex-side-down?
questions.n: A mission (barrel) tile roof uses separate semi-cylindrical pan-and-cover tiles laid in courses with the convex side alternating up and down.

questions.q: Which property below best describes stone?
questions.n:
Stone is generally isotropic — its properties are essentially the same in every direction, unlike a grained material such as wood. iso-: 

Derived from the Ancient Greek word isos (ἴσος), meaning "equal" or "same".-tropic / tropos: Derived from the Ancient Greek word tropos (τρόπος) from trepein (τρεῖν), meaning "to turn," "direction," or "way".

Turning or facing equally in all directions.

questions.q: What is the term for visible waviness or distortion on a flat metal panel's surface, sometimes caused by manufacturing stress, overtightened fasteners, thermal movement, or handling?
questions.n: "Oil-canning" describes visible waviness or distortion on the flat surface of a metal panel or sheet.

questions.q: When a specification provision requires the Contractor to take an action, which word signals that requirement?
questions.n: "Shall" is the standard word used in specifications to impose a mandatory requirement on the Contractor.

questions.q: Which type of lockset cannot be mounted into the edge of a door?
questions.n: A rim lock mounts on the face of the door with its case sitting on the surface, so unlike mortise or cylinder locks it is never installed into or through the door edge.

questions.q: In the roof identification figure, point "E" marks the small triangular wall area under a gable roof end. What is it called?
questions.n: The triangular wall section formed under the end of a gable roof is the gable — visible at the dormer's gable end, point E.

questions.q: What is the continuous wire support called that holds reinforcing bars near the bottom of a slab?
questions.n: In CRSI bar-support terminology, a "bolster" is a continuous, semi-circular wire support used specifically to hold bottom bars in slabs; individual "chairs" typically support bars in beams or isolated spots.

questions.q: For that same mix, a water-cement ratio of 0.58 was specified. How much mixing water does that require?
questions.n: Water needed = w/c ratio × cement weight = 0.58 × (15 bags × 40 kg) = 0.58 × 600 kg ≈ 348 liters, which rounds to about 350 liters (1 kg water ≈ 1 liter).

questions.q: What describes a flat or pitched truss where the vertical members carry tension and the diagonals carry compression?
questions.n: In a Howe truss, verticals are in tension and diagonals are in compression — the opposite arrangement of a Pratt truss.

questions.q: What produces the visible growth rings seen in a cross-section of a tree trunk?
questions.n: The denser, darker latewood (summerwood) band of each year's growth is what makes the rings visually stand out in cross-section.

questions.q: A naturally weathering metal must form its own protective oxide layer strong enough to handle typical roof exposure. Which metal below does NOT do this?
questions.n: Carbon steel just rusts progressively instead of forming a stable, adherent protective layer, unlike aluminum, copper, and lead, which each build a natural protective patina or oxide film.

questions.q: What is it called when design and construction phases are deliberately overlapped to shorten a project's total schedule?
questions.n: "Fast-tracking" means overlapping design and construction phases so the overall project duration is compressed.

questions.q: Diaphragm action is the bracing effect a thin, rigid plane provides when loaded parallel to that plane. Which of these does NOT work this way?
questions.n: Diaphragm action needs a solid, continuous plane (wall panels, metal decking, or a basement/shear wall) resisting in-plane loads. A truss is an open, skeletal frame, not a solid diaphragm.

questions.q: In the roof identification figure, point "I" marks a sloped trim piece along a gable end. What is it called?
questions.n: The sloped trim running along a gable end’s roof edge is the rake, shown along the dormer’s gable edge at point I.

questions.q: Which of these rock types is metamorphic?
questions.n: Marble is metamorphic — it forms when limestone recrystallizes under heat and pressure.

questions.q: Controlled Low-Strength Material (CLSM) — a self-compacting cementitious slurry used instead of compacted soil backfill — is also commonly known by what other name?
questions.n: "Flowable fill" is the everyday industry name for CLSM, a self-consolidating slurry poured in place of compacted soil backfill.

questions.q: When a specification simply states information about actions the Owner will take, which word is used?
questions.n: "Will" is reserved for informational statements about the Owner's (or the Owner's separate contractors') actions, distinct from the Contractor's mandatory "shall" obligations.

questions.q: What do you call a tall, narrow fixed window mounted next to a door?
questions.n: A tall, narrow fixed pane flanking a door opening is called a sidelight.
